rows.label: The Levites, the priests and the singers

doors.name: To give thanks and to praise the LORD

eg.text: David appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to celebrate, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.

The trumpeters and singers joined together to praise and thank the LORD with one voice. They lifted up their voices, accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, in praise to the LORD: “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” And the temple, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud

The priests stood at their posts, as did the Levites with the musical instruments of the LORD, which King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD and with which David had offered praise, saying, “For His loving devotion endures forever.” Across from the Levites, the priests sounded trumpets, and all the Israelites were standing.

In keeping with the ordinances of his father David, Solomon appointed the divisions of the priests over their service, and the Levites for their duties to offer praise and to minister before the priests according to the daily requirement. He also appointed gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate, for this had been the command of David, the man of God.

rows.label: They glorified God, praised God, sang hymns to God
rows.note: In most of these the Greek verb is δοξάζω, “glorify”; a few are αἰνέω, “praise”, or ὑμνέω, “sing a hymn”. They are different words, and in Luke 2:20 and 18:43 the text sets two of them side by side.

eg.text: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
And they glorified God because of me.
The crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.
And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”

rows.label: “Glorify God,” “glorify Your name,” “that God may be glorified”

eg.text: In the same way, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.

rows.label: Jesus glorified, the Father glorified, and who glorifies whom (John, Acts, Hebrews, Luke 4:15)
rows.note: Here the Greek is δοξάζω, “glorify”, the glory card's verb. It is also the verb of “they glorified God”, but the page does not treat the Father and the Son glorifying one another as praise, or as the same act as a crowd glorifying God. John 16:14 is the Spirit glorifying Jesus. Where Christian traditions part on how the persons glorify one another, the page takes no side.

eg.text: He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

rows.label: Praise given to someone or something other than the LORD: a king, a wife, a manager, their gods

eg.text: When Pharaoh's officials saw Sarai, they commended her to him, and she was taken into the palace of Pharaoh.

As they drank the wine, they praised their gods of gold and silver, bronze and iron, wood and stone.

The vessels from His house were brought to you, and as you drank wine from them with your nobles, wives, and concubines, you praised your gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or understand. But you have failed to glorify the God who holds in His hand your very breath and all your ways.

rows.label: The dead do not praise
rows.note: Ps 6:5, 30:9 and 88:10 say the same with the thanks word יָדָה, which the Berean also prints “praise”; see Other words.

doors.name: Who can praise You from Sheol?

eg.text: It is not the dead who praise the LORD, nor any who descend into silence.
For Sheol cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who descend to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.

rows.label: Knew God and did not glorify Him as God or give thanks

eg.text: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.

rows.label: Glorified: the word of the Lord, those He justified, oneself, what was once glorious
rows.note: None of these is praise offered to God. They are here only because the Greek verb is the same, δοξάζω, “glorify”. Rom 8:30 and Acts 13:48 are listed for that verb alone; the page takes no side on how their other words (“predestined”, “appointed”) are read. Here the one glorified is the word of the Lord, those He justified, oneself (Rev 18:7), or what was once glorious (2 Cor 3:10, the ministry whose glory has been surpassed).
